islamic_reference.note: Cousin and son-in-law of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), fourth Caliph

historical_references.reference: Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf Al-Thaqafi appointed 'Amr ibn Al-'Aas his governor of Egypt in 683 CE. 'Amr established a mosque and named it after his daughter, Aliaa.
historical_references.context: The Umayyad Caliphate, Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf Al-Thaqafi's rule

historical_references.reference: The Fatimid Caliphate (909-1171 CE) used Aliaa as an alternative name for their female rulers. Al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah (r. 996-1021 CE) had a daughter named Aliaa Khatun.
